title: Session Customizations
intro:
This prototype explores a clearer division between two customization surfaces in the Agents window.

**Session Customizations** is the scoped right sidebar for the active session. It surfaces the high-value customizations people may want to quickly inspect or toggle for that session: Plugins, MCP Servers, and Connectors.

The global **Customizations** modal is for viewing and managing the complete customization inventory across agent harnesses, workspaces, and environments. In particular, please try the sentence-style scope controls: **View {customization type} for {harness} in {workspace} across {environment}**.

Please focus feedback on the relationship and distinction between these two surfaces, the right sidebar’s contents, and the modal’s scope controls. Customization detail-page content is intentionally omitted from this prototype.
questions: Does “Session Customizations” clearly communicate that the right sidebar is scoped to the active session, and are Plugins, MCP Servers, and Connectors the right high-value items to surface there?
Do the “View {type} for {harness} in {workspace} across {environment}” controls make the global modal’s scope and filtering model understandable?
Is the relationship between Session Customizations and the global Customizations modal clear? What, if anything, still feels ambiguous?

items.label: Session Customizations
items.note: Use the Session Activity Bar’s Session Customizations entry to inspect the scoped sidebar. Use the left sidebar’s Customizations entry to open the global modal and try its harness, workspace, and environment scope controls.
